nodes.title: the Ponmi signature
nodes.statement: The Ponmi system concerns objects called vashumbs. There are exactly 5 of them: korrvex, keldclo, glimsib, hobtez, korrdri. Two operations are written ? and &. One relation is written %%, read as "governs".

nodes.title: the Ponmi combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x ? y for every pair of vashumbs is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for &. The pairs standing in the %% relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x and y, x ? y is again a vashumb.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x and y, x & y is again a vashumb.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x, y, z: (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x and y: x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a vashumb korrvex with korrvex & x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every vashumb x: x & x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every vashumb x: x %% x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x and y: if x %% y and y %% x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x, y, z: if x %% y and y %% z then x %% z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x and y, at least one of x %% y and y %% x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all vashumbs x, y, z: if x %% y then (z & x) %% (z & y) and (x & z) %% (y & z).

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all vashumbs x, y, z: (x ? y) ? z = x ? (y ? z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = keldclo, y = korrvex, z = keldclo, left = korrvex, right = keldclo, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: tarnmux vashumbs
nodes.statement: A vashumb x is called tarnmux when x ? x = x.

nodes.title: vashumbs that yukdri
nodes.statement: Two vashumbs x and y are said to yukdri when x ? y = y ? x.

nodes.title: hurnisk collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of vashumbs is hurnisk when x ? y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the brasib of a vashumb
nodes.statement: The brasib of a vashumb x is the collection of vashumbs y for which x %% y holds.

nodes.title: the yukfex
nodes.statement: The yukfex of the system is the collection of vashumbs that yukdri with every vashumb.

nodes.title: the mimorn
nodes.statement: The mimorn is the collection of all tarnmux vashumbs.

nodes.title: the reldmi of a vashumb
nodes.statement: The reldmi of a vashumb x, written [x], is the smallest hurnisk collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a vexlum
nodes.statement: A vashumb f is a vexlum when f %% y holds for every vashumb y, that is, when the brasib of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the vorzam of a vashumb
nodes.statement: The vorzam of a vashumb x is the number of vashumbs in its reldmi [x].

nodes.title: the fexpon
nodes.statement: The fexpon of the system is the collection of vashumbs whose vorzam is largest.

nodes.title: ovijen pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct vashumbs x and y form a ovijen pair when x %% y and y %% x both hold, that is, when each lies in the brasib of the other.

nodes.title: the reldmi of a vashumb is hurnisk
nodes.statement: For every vashumb x, the collection [x] is hurnisk.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under ?.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the reldmi is contained in every hurnisk collection
nodes.statement: If S is hurnisk and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a vashumb is tarnmux exactly when its vorzam is one
nodes.statement: x ? x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x ? x = x then {x} is already closed under ?.
So [x] = {x} and the vorzam is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x ? x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the vorzam divides the number of vashumbs breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every vashumb x, the vorzam of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = keldclo, reach = 2, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the mimorn is hurnisk
nodes.statement: If x and y are both tarnmux then so is x ? y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be tarnmux.
The claim asks whether (x ? y) ? (x ? y) returns x ? y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: brasibs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the brasib of x, then the brasib of y is contained in the brasib of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x %% y and let z satisfy y %% z.
Transitivity gives x %% z.
So every member of the brasib of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one vexlum
nodes.statement: No two distinct vashumbs can both be vexlums.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f %% h, since h is any object, and h %% f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a vexlum
nodes.statement: Some vashumb vexlums the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no ovijen pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct vashumbs lie in each other's brasib.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
